original_excerpt:
From Terry v. Ohio, 392 U.S. 1, 30–31 (1968):
"We merely hold today that where a police officer observes unusual conduct which leads him reasonably to conclude in light of his experience that criminal activity may be afoot and that the persons with whom he is dealing may be armed and presently dangerous... he is entitled for the protection of himself and others in the area to conduct a carefully limited search of the outer clothing of such persons in an attempt to discover weapons... Such a search is a reasonable search under the Fourth Amendment, and any weapons seized may properly be introduced in evidence against the person from whom they were taken."   
From Mapp v. Ohio, 367 U.S. 643, 655 (1961):
"We hold that all evidence obtained by searches and seizures in violation of the Constitution is, by that same authority, inadmissible in a state court."
fidelity: Terry and Mapp quoted wording corresponds; Terry interior ellipsis removes self-identification/inquiries and failure to dispel reasonable fear conditions.
scope_note: Retain armed-and-dangerous grounds and carefully limited weapons frisk. Ellipsis should not be used to remove those intervening conditions in a substantive account; not authority for general evidence searches.
